institution: National Centre for Disease Control, National AMR Surveillance Network (NARS-Net)
citation: National Centre for Disease Control. Annual Report: Surveillance of Priority Bacterial Pathogens under National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network, 2018. New Delhi: National Programme on Antimicrobial Resistance Containment, NCDC; 2019.
reporting: Percent resistant (%R, whole numbers) with number tested, by pathogen for blood, urine, pus aspirates with other sterile body fluids (one combined column) and pooled all-specimen columns, all location types combined; location bar charts (outpatient, inpatient, ICU) with printed data labels and the number of isolates per location.
method: WHONET; data validated and analysed at NCDC; 50,724 isolates from unique patients reported by 16 sentinel sites (medical colleges) in 14 states. AST method and breakpoint standard not stated. Colistin results for E. coli, Klebsiella and Acinetobacter were not considered (not tested by broth microdilution); Pseudomonas colistin by broth microdilution for 45 isolates; S. aureus vancomycin by broth microdilution for 14 isolates.

verification.note: Tables 4 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber extract_tables, cross-checked with the PyMuPDF text dump; grey cells placed from the page image) and every value (number tested and %R) then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 and with zoomed crops of each table at scale 3. In every pooled column the numbers tested equal the sum of the specimen columns (except nitrofurantoin, noted). Table 2 counts transcribed from the text layer, compared with the page and checked against its row and column totals (50,724). The figures quoted in the report text agree with the tables except Acinetobacter amikacin and gentamicin (recorded as conflicts). Location charts (Figures 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b, 8a, 8b, 9, 10, 11, 12) are raster images with no text layer: the data labels were read from the embedded images enlarged 1.6 to 1.8 times, and each label was checked against its bar by measuring the bar lengths in pixels (bars detected by colour at the common axis, a pixels-per-percent scale fitted per chart): every one of the 225 labels matches its bar within 0.2 percentage points, and the bar colour sequence in each group (light blue, grey, dark blue) matches the legend order outpatient, inpatient, ICU, confirmed from the legend squares of every chart. Each pooled table value lies within the range of its location labels except Klebsiella blood ertapenem (noted). Page numbers are PDF page numbers (1-based).

notes: Second NARS-Net annual report: 16 sentinel sites (medical colleges) in 14 states (20 laboratories in 18 states in the network by March 2019), seven priority pathogens, 1 January to 31 December 2018. All figures are percent resistant, printed as whole numbers. As in 2017, pus aspirates and other sterile body fluids are one combined column ("PA+OSBF"), shown here as pus; the pooled "Blood + Pus Aspirate + OSBF" columns are shown as all specimens except urine (S. aureus, Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter were not collected from urine, so for them this is every specimen under surveillance) and the columns that add urine as all specimens. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows come from bar charts with printed data labels and the number of isolates per location in the legend (Figures 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b, 8a, 8b, 9, 10, 11 and 12); "Inpatient" (IPD in Table 3, non-ICU inpatients) is shown as wards. Figures 8a, 8b, 11 and 12 do not name the specimens; their legend N equal the Table 3 location counts over all specimens of that pathogen, so they are recorded as all specimens (E. coli, Klebsiella) or all specimens except urine (Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter). S. Typhi and S. Paratyphi are reported separately (Table 10; S. Paratyphi n=23). Colistin results for E. coli, Klebsiella and Acinetobacter were not considered by the report. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (the printed page number is one less).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 102 of 406 cells (48 table cells, 54 chart labels) was read from the page images before the extracted values were looked at, then every other cell as well: all 406 cells (181 table cells with their numbers tested, 225 chart labels), all 53 row n and all 17 Table 2 counts. Tables rendered at scale 2.5 and cropped at scale 3.5; the ten location charts (raster images without a text layer) extracted from the PDF at native resolution and enlarged 2 to 2.25 times. 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Second reader, chart rows: in all ten charts the legend squares run light blue, grey, dark blue from the top beside Outpatient, Inpatient, ICU, and every bar group runs in the same colour order from the top. A script measured every bar by colour from the common axis: each of my 225 label readings matches the length of its bar within 0.2 percentage points on a scale fitted per chart. Drug of each group read from its axis label; the legend N of every chart equal the row n.

Second reader, charts that do not name the specimen (Figures 8a, 8b, 11, 12): the legend N equal the Table 3 location counts of the pathogen exactly (E. coli 6,265, 10,465, 716; Klebsiella 2,111, 4,941, 1,306; Pseudomonas 894, 1,823, 344; Acinetobacter 473, 2,351, 1,001), whose sums are the Table 3 totals over all specimens and exceed every single specimen column of Table 2. The means of the location labels weighted by these N also reproduce the pooled table columns (mean difference 0.3, 0.8, 0.7 and 0.9 points) better than any single specimen column (0.8 to 8.0 points). The mapping to all (E. coli, Klebsiella) and nonurine (Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter) is sound. Figure 4a legend N also equal the S. aureus Table 3 counts.

Second reader, cells not kept: the two caution cells are printed as recorded. Table 9 (PDF page 16) prints Acinetobacter amikacin 68% of 3,272 and gentamicin 56% of 2,335 in the Blood + Pus Aspirate + OSBF column, while the text on PDF page 14 says amikacin 66% and gentamicin 54%. The table figures agree with their own specimen columns (amikacin 74% and 61% of 1,636 each, 67.5%; gentamicin 66% of 1,183 and 46% of 1,152, 56.1%) and with Figure 12 (weighted 68.9% and 56.5%), so the text is the outlier: a source contradiction, conflicts kept. No count-table mismatches are listed.

Second reader: the other row notes are accurate: nitrofurantoin pooled numbers tested (E. coli 13,358 against 13,194 in urine; Klebsiella 4,019 against 3,799) beside grey blood and PA+OSBF cells; Klebsiella blood ertapenem 60% above all three Figure 10 labels (50, 57, 59), the only pooled table value outside the range of its location labels; S. aureus vancomycin tested in 14, 11 and 3 isolates; Pseudomonas colistin in 45, 28 and 17; S. Typhi imipenem 13% of 53 and S. Paratyphi imipenem 0 of 1. Every other figure quoted in the text (PDF pages 6, 7, 10, 14 and 17) matches the tables. Metadata confirmed on PDF pages 2 and 4 (16 sentinel sites in 14 states, 50,724 isolates, 1 January to 31 December 2018).

Lead 2026-09-26: the combined "pus aspirate + other sterile body fluids" column filed under specimen "deep" (deep infections, aspirates), as for the other NCDC-protocol reports; specimen as printed is kept on each row; 9 rows and 6 counts moved from "pus".
